input: Fact-check my Wikipedia article draft before publishing

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Wikipedia articles vary enormously — a stub has 10 claims to check, a featured-article-length draft might have 300. Knowing the length and density of claims sets the scale of the whole effort.
Is this a solo check, or will multiple editors/reviewers be involved? That changes whether the process needs a shared tracking system or just a personal checklist.
The subject domain (science, biography, history, pop culture, etc.) determines which authoritative sources are credible and which fact-checking methods apply.
A deadline (e.g., needs to go live tomorrow vs. no rush) directly sets how thorough the fact-checking can realistically be.
Wikipedia has specific citation policies (WP:V, WP:RS). Knowing whether the user wants to align strictly with Wikipedia sourcing rules vs. just general accuracy changes what counts as a valid source.
Does the user want every sentence sourced, or only flagged claims that seem contestable? The bar for 'done' shapes the entire review process.
Knowing the format of the draft (Google Doc, wiki sandbox, plain text paste, etc.) determines the immediate first step and what tools or workflows are practical.

gold.taskTitle: Fact-check Wikipedia article draft before publishing
gold.taskDescription: Review a Wikipedia article draft to verify factual accuracy across all claims before it goes live.

questions.title: How long is the draft, roughly how many claims?
questions.description: Understand the scale of the article — stub, mid-length, or comprehensive — to size the fact-checking effort correctly.

questions.title: What subject or topic does the article cover?
questions.description: Identify the domain (e.g., science, biography, history) so the right authoritative sources and subject-matter methods can be applied.

questions.title: Are you fact-checking alone or with other editors?
questions.description: Determine whether the process needs a shared tracking system or a simple personal checklist.

questions.title: When does the article need to be published?
questions.description: Establish the deadline to calibrate how thorough and systematic the fact-checking process can realistically be.

questions.title: Should sources meet Wikipedia's Reliable Sources policy strictly?
questions.description: Clarify whether verification must follow Wikipedia's formal sourcing rules (WP:RS, WP:V) or a broader general-accuracy standard.

questions.title: What does a fully fact-checked draft look like to you?
questions.description: Define the finish line — e.g., every sentence cited, only contested claims flagged, or a structured report of issues found.

questions.title: Where does the draft currently live, in what format?
questions.description: Identify the tool or location (Wikipedia sandbox, Google Doc, plain text, etc.) to determine the immediate first action and practical workflow.
